newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sorghum market remains steady-Grainco.
newsitem.headline: Australia sorghum market remains steady-Grainco.

text.p: Australia's domestic sorghum prices traded sideways in southern Queensland in the past week amid little activity from growers and consumers,

Values in central Queensland were steady to slightly higher because of a slight strengthening in U.S. corn futures, Rob Brealey, trading manager of Queensland co-operative Grainco Ltd, said in his weekly market report.

The U.S. corn crop, estimated as the third largest in history, could weaken the international market. But old crop stocks were at one of the lowest levels ever and problems with progress and development will cause a market reaction, he said.

Values remained steady in the southern Queensland at around A$143.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane for June. Limited tonnage had traded at this level with growers waiting for the new financial year or concentrating on winter planting.

In central Queensland, values finished the week around $121.00 a tonne delivered port, with the short-term focus U.S. corn crop progress. Corn crop problems would be supportive for short to medium-term Australian sorghum, Brealey said.
New crop values remain supported with continued concerns about the damage to parts of the European crop, particularly in Spain and France.

With harvesting in Europe to start in around three weeks, the market will wait for yield results. This, together with Australian barley plantings delayed because of drought, supported current values, he said.

Domestic feed barley values finished the week unchanged at A$175.0 a tonne for old crop delivered Brisbane, still reflecting a premium over export values which remain at around US$145.00 a tonne fob. New crop values finished the week around A$153.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane for November-December.

The lack of substantial planting rains in Australia has maintained stability in the international malting barley market. International demand for malting barley is traditionally low at this time of the year and a significant increase in demand is not expected until October or November. Domestic new crop malting barley remains around A$183.00 a tonne delivered port.

With the containerised cottonseed market in a lull, activity has been focused on the conclusion of additional bulk export business. After months of negotiation parcels of bulk cottonseed have now been committed to export.
Encouraging interest in the supply of bulk cottonseed is emerging from Europe and North America.
As production increases over the coming years new outlets for Australian cottonseed will be required in order to maintain acceptable price levels.
While scope for growth existed in containerised cottonseed, particularly in Asia, it would be limited, he said.

Shipment of bulk cottonseed opened a range of new marketing opportunities for Australian seed, especially with Australian seed supply counter-cyclical to northern hemisphere production. Export enquiries persist but at levels up to US$10.00 a tonne

below where business was being concluded a month ago. Japanese cottonseed consumers still believe prices will weaken becaused of the large crop. Despite this cash prices continue to trade A$145.00 to A$150.00 a tonne Downs gin.
Central Queensland domestic prices remain steady at A$145.00 to $150.00 a tonne ex gin for the ginning period.

Very little activity occurred in the pulse market in the past week, he said. Planting continues in northern New South Wales (NSW) and southern Queensland as ground dries following recent rains. Growers in many areas of central Queensland await further rains in order to continue pulse planting.
New crop price indications remain around A$310.00 to $315.00 a tonne delivered port for Queensland chickpeas and around A$250.00 a tonne port for new crop faba beans.
